name: Cartalax
storage: Store at -20 °C, protected from light and moisture.
definition: Cartalax (AED) is a linear synthetic peptide supplied as white lyophilized powder. The catalogue lists 1 pack size: 20 mg. The CAS number, full sequence and molecular weight are recorded in the lot-specific certificate of analysis (COA). Purity is stated at ≥99.0% (HPLC) with white lyophilized powder appearance. Each kit contains 10 vials; minimum order quantity is 1 kit. Store the lyophilized powder at -20 °C, protected from light and moisture. For laboratory research use only; not for human or veterinary use.

faq.question: How is Cartalax tested for purity and identity?
faq.answer: Each AED lot is run on RP-HPLC against a ≥99.0% (HPLC) release limit, then confirmed by MS. The batch certificate carries the measured purity, retention time and mass together with the identity string (CAS 85806-95-7, formula C12H19N3O8, 333.29 Da).

faq.question: How should Cartalax be stored?
faq.answer: Dry powder for Cartalax: store at −20 °C. Working solution: 2–8 °C, used within the window printed on the AED lot certificate.

faq.question: What pack sizes are available for Cartalax?
faq.answer: Cartalax is stocked in 1 pack size (20 mg), 10 vials per kit, MOQ 1 kit. At 1–9 kits the per-kit price is $105.84; 10–49 kits falls to $97.38 (−8%) and 50+ to $89.96 (−15%).

compliance: For Research, Laboratory, and Analytical Use Only. Not for Human or Veterinary Use.
